regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% looks like acceleration — until you note the RBI's own forecast sits at 6.6%, a 120bps gap that implies the statistical office and the central bank are reading different economies. IIP at 6.7% and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% from 75.6% are genuine — but PMI manufacturing slipped to 52.8 from 53.5, and core sector decelerated to 5.4% from 6.0%. The quality of this growth is uneven: services PMI at 54.5 is doing the heavy lifting while the goods economy quietly softens.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 27.41%","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% is manageable; decompose it and the picture sharpens uncomfortably. Core at 3.9% is benign, but food at 5.52% is rising and fuel at 27.41% — still the 100th percentile of a decade — has only eased from 30.33%, not resolved. RBI's own inflation forecast has moved up to 5.1% from 4.6% — a 50bps revision that sits awkwardly alongside a repo cut cycle. If Brent holds near $97 and food inflation doesn't break, the RBI will find itself having cut into a supply-side inflation problem it cannot solve with rates.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 13.8%; CD 83.04%","signal_text":"CD ratio at 83.04% — up from 82.5% and at the 81st percentile of a decade — is the structural fault line. NBFC credit growth has decelerated sharply to 13% from 17% YoY, and corporate bond issuance surging to ₹1,12,000 cr at a 7th-percentile level signals that borrowers are being pushed into capital markets because bank deposit funding is scarce. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% through a rate-cut cycle was FY14 — within 12 months, the taper tantrum forced an emergency reversal. Reserves are higher today, but the structural tension is identical.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% — down from 5.50% — puts the real rate at roughly 80bps against headline CPI, thin enough to be accommodative but not so loose as to alarm. For housing, the average home loan rate falling to 8.12% from 8.5% is already feeding disbursements up 13.6% to ₹2,59,000 cr. The risk is that the RBI is cutting while its own inflation forecast rises — a contradiction that either resolves through a pause or, if Brent stays at $97+, through an embarrassing reversal.","badge_label":"Easing Cycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% — the 74th percentile — make the capex upcycle case credible, not aspirational. Credit to industry growing at 20% YoY (78th percentile) and credit to services at 22.9% (76th percentile) confirm that working capital and investment borrowing are both expanding. The inversion worth watching: private capex historically accelerates above 80% capacity utilisation — at 77.4%, India is close but not there, which means the next two quarters of utilisation data will determine whether this is a genuine private investment cycle or a public-capex-led mirage.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 200640; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,00,640 cr — 71st percentile — is strong, but the composition matters more than the headline. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheelers at 19.7% suggest both urban and rural demand are participating, a broader base than the affluent-only story of recent quarters. Airline passengers at 86.4 mn (35th percentile) tell a different story — discretionary travel is not keeping pace with goods consumption. E-commerce GMV growth at 18% (26th percentile) is the quiet warning: digital consumption, the bellwether of urban middle-class spending, is running well below its historical norm.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 13.8% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 300bps divergence widening for consecutive months (CD ratio 83.04%, up from 82.5%). NBFC credit growth has decelerated sharply to 13% from 17% YoY, signalling funding stress. Corporate bond issuance surged to ₹112,000 cr (vs ₹106,000 cr prior), a 10-year low percentile (7%), indicating forced capital market reliance as deposit funding dries up.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they will poach deposits from weaker peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will spike. Duration plays benefit from RBI's easing cycle (repo at 5.25%, down 25bps), but credit quality deteriorates for sub-investment-grade corporates forced into bond markets at higher yields. Reduce exposure to mid-tier housing finance companies.","pct_10y":81,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 81st percentile (10-year high) — last time this was breached, RBI tightened liquidity and smaller banks faced deposit runs. This regime preceded a 200bps widening in NBFC-bank credit spreads.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Firmly Entrenched","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16% YoY (latest), capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6%), and core sector growth at 5.4% YoY. India's FY GDP estimate revised up to 7.6% (80th percentile, 10-year high). PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile), with services PMI at 54.5 (up from 53.3), signalling broad-based demand. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (78th percentile) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (76th percentile) confirm capex and working capital expansion.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Increase allocation to project-linked companies (EPC, infrastructure). Private capex is leading; public capex remains steady. Favour companies with order books >2 years and ROCE >15%. Avoid cyclical consumer discretionary — capex demand is crowding out consumption credit (personal credit at 16.2% YoY, only 51st percentile). Expect margin pressure in Q4 as input costs (WPI at 9.78%, down from 9.87% but still elevated) persist.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 74th percentile signals mid-cycle expansion, not overheating. Historically, this level preceded 18-24 months of sustained capex before mean reversion.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 91st Percentile","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹31,961 cr (latest), up from ₹31,781 cr, with YoY growth at 19.85% (up from 15.84%). SIP AUM at ₹18.2 tr (91st percentile, 10-year high), but SIP accounts at 9.9 cr (only 2nd percentile, 10-year low). MF AUM at ₹85.76 tr (85th percentile), with equity MF net inflows at ₹24,697 cr (down from ₹28,973 cr). Equity MF net flows are decelerating despite SIP strength.","implication":"SIP accounts growing 2.7% YoY but AUM growing 6.3% — average ticket size is rising sharply. This is affluent money entering, not mass retail. Retail equity participation is concentrating among HNI/UHNI segments. Favour large-cap, dividend-paying stocks (Nifty 50 down 0.5% but Bank Nifty at 57,088, 94th percentile). Reduce exposure to small/mid-cap growth stories; retail is rotating to safety. Watch for SIP account growth to inflect — if it stays <5% YoY, mass retail is exiting.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 91st percentile is a late-cycle indicator. Historically, when SIP AUM reaches this level, equity returns compress 12-18 months later as retail capitulates.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Remains Structural Threat","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 27.41% YoY (down from 30.33% but still at 100th percentile, 10-year extreme). Brent crude at $97.21/bbl (68th percentile), up from $88.82 six months ago. WTI at $92.61/bbl (78th percentile). Natural gas at $2.98/MMBtu (18th percentile, 10-year low), but copper at $6.72/lb (80th percentile, 10-year high) and iron ore at $161.91/mt (63rd percentile). CPI headline at 4.45% (41st percentile) but food inflation at 5.52% (48th percentile) — both rising.","implication":"Fuel inflation remains a structural headwind for RBI's inflation target (5.1% forecast, up from 4.6%). This limits further rate cuts — expect repo to hold at 5.25% for 2-3 quarters. Overweight energy stocks (oil majors, refiners) and underweight consumer staples with low pricing power. Hedge INR weakness via commodity exposure. India's CAD will widen if oil stays >$95/bbl; monitor FII flows for signs of stress. Avoid long-duration bonds — inflation expectations are sticky.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 100th percentile is a 10-year extreme. Last time fuel inflation was this high (2022), RBI hiked rates 190bps in 6 months and equity markets corrected 25%.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"Fed Holds, BOJ Tightens, Carry Unwinds","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). US 10Y Treasury at 4.77% (down 2bps, but 86th percentile, 10-year high) — recent trend shows 4 of last 5 weeks up, signalling sticky long-end yields. BOJ rate at 1.0% (up from 0.75%, 86th percentile, 10-year high), a strong-negative signal (-72 score). ECB deposit rate at 2.25% (up from 2.0%). US GDP at 1.5% SAAR (down from 2.1%), US PMI composite at 56 (84th percentile, 10-year high). Global PMI at 53.5 (82nd percentile).","implication":"BOJ tightening is the key risk. Yen carry trades are unwinding — watch USD/JPY for breaks below 145. This will trigger risk-off flows globally, including from India. US 10Y at 4.77% (86th percentile) is a ceiling for Indian yields; any move higher will attract FII outflows. FII equity net is already negative at -₹3,111.94 cr. Reduce duration exposure in India; favour short-end bonds (1-3Y). Equity valuations are vulnerable if US yields spike above 5%. Hedge via long INR (carry unwind favours INR) or short Nifty 50 calls.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 86th percentile and BOJ at 86th percentile simultaneously is rare. This regime preceded the 2018 emerging market crisis and the 2022 equity correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"INR Weakens as Carry Unwinds","data_text":"INR/USD at 94.34 (flat, but 87th percentile, 10-year high weakness). Recent trend: 95.24→96.15→95.24→96.15→95.24→94.34 (volatile, 2 of last 5 weeks up). DXY at 99.176 (flat, 47th percentile), but recent trend shows 2 of last 5 weeks up. India VIX at 11.16 (up from 10.68, 6th percentile, 10-year low volatility). Brent at $97.21 (68th percentile) pressures CAD. Home loan disbursements at ₹259,000 cr (up from ₹228,000 cr), suggesting domestic demand remains resilient but import-intensive.","implication":"INR at 87th percentile weakness is a yellow flag. If BOJ carry unwinds accelerate, INR could breach 95.5 quickly. RBI will likely intervene to defend 95.5 — watch for reserve depletion signals. FII outflows (-₹3,111.94 cr equity) are a leading indicator of INR stress. Overweight INR hedges (long INR forwards, short USD/INR calls). Reduce exposure to import-heavy sectors (autos, electronics). Favour exporters (IT, pharma, textiles). Monitor RBI's forward guidance on intervention — any signal of passivity will trigger a 200-300pips INR move.","pct_10y":87,"pct_note":"INR at 87th percentile weakness coincides with BOJ tightening and US 10Y at 86th percentile. This is a carry unwind regime; historically, INR weakens 3-5% in such cycles before stabilising.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Rents Soar While Absorption Collapses","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.7 mn sqft (up from 13.05 mn sqft, but 6th percentile, 10-year low) — a strong-negative signal (-88 score). Yet office rents in Bengaluru at ₹163/sqft (up from ₹148, 95th percentile, 10-year high) and Mumbai at ₹335/sqft (up from ₹322, 100th percentile, 10-year extreme). Office vacancy at 14.7% (down from 15.2%, 43rd percentile). Nifty 50 down 0.5% YoY, IT services credit growth at 22.9% YoY (76th percentile), but IT stock valuations flat. Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (down from 11.6%, 35th percentile, 10-year low).","implication":"This is a GCC (Global Capability Centre) story, not traditional IT services. Multinational corporates are consolidating office footprints (low absorption) but paying premium rents for prime locations (Bengaluru, Mumbai). Traditional IT services companies are NOT the marginal buyer — they're shedding space post-pandemic. Overweight commercial real estate (Embassy, Mindspace) and underweight Nifty IT. The IT sector's credit growth (22.9%) is masking a structural shift: GCCs are hiring, but IT services are automating. This explains why IT stock valuations are flat despite 22.9% credit growth. Falsifiable: If Nifty IT outperforms Nifty 50 by >500bps in next 6 months, this thesis is wrong. If office rents in Tier-2 cities (Pune, Hyderabad) remain flat while Bengaluru/Mumbai rents rise, GCC consolidation is confirmed.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile (10-year low) while rents hit 95-100th percentile is a regime shift. Historically, this divergence preceded a 15-20% correction in IT services stocks and a 25-30% outperformance of commercial real estate REITs.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a 6.6% RBI forecast is not a rounding error — it is a 120bps institutional disagreement about what is actually happening in the economy. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) flatters on the surface; manufacturing at 52.8 is softening while services at 54.5 carries the load — a services-led expansion that historically proves more fragile when global demand slows. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is rising and IIP capital goods at 16% YoY is genuine, but core sector deceleration to 5.4% from 6.0% suggests the goods economy is not uniformly confirming the headline. GST at ₹2,00,640 cr and two-wheeler sales at 19.7% are the two proxies that keep the consumption story credible — watch both for any sequential softening.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US GDP at 1.5% SAAR — down from 2.1% — is slowing while US PMI composite hits 56 (84th percentile), a divergence that usually resolves in the PMI's direction with a lag, or exposes the PMI as a sentiment survey rather than an activity measure. BOJ at 1.0% (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is the structural shift the market keeps underpricing — every 25bps from Tokyo tightens global yen carry and pressures EM assets that benefited from it. US 10Y at 4.77% has risen four of the last five periods; the Fed is on hold at 3.63% while the long end prices its own verdict on fiscal sustainability. China at 4.7% GDP and 0.5% CPI is the deflationary anchor that keeps global goods prices suppressed — until it isn't.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP inflows at ₹31,961 cr (91st percentile) are structurally robust, but equity MF net flows fell to ₹24,697 cr from ₹28,973 cr — a ₹4,276 cr sequential decline that suggests lump-sum investors are stepping back even as SIP automation holds. FII equity net at -₹3,112 cr against DII net of +₹8,930 cr means domestic institutions are absorbing foreign selling — a pattern that can persist until DII dry powder thins. Corporate bond issuance at ₹1,12,000 cr (7th percentile) signals that credit-constrained borrowers are paying up for capital market access as the CD ratio at 83.04% leaves banks with limited deposit headroom. INR at 94.34 (87th percentile) has stabilised after oscillating between 94.34 and 96.15 over five periods — the calm is real but the range is not reassuring.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty 50 at 23,779 (76th percentile) has risen only once in the last five sessions — a market that is not falling but is not finding conviction either, with Bank Nifty at 57,088 (94th percentile) carrying valuation risk if NIM compression follows from deposit rate competition. Office rents in Mumbai at ₹335/sqft (100th percentile) and Bengaluru at ₹163/sqft (95th percentile) are at decade extremes — yet absorption at 13.7 mn sqft sits at the 6th percentile, and REIT prices tell the real story: Embassy down to ₹369.92 from ₹438.69, Mindspace to ₹345.06 from ₹501.11. Residential real estate launches at a 0th-percentile 106,000 units and sales at 90,715 units (0th percentile) with unsold inventory rising to 6,16,000 units suggest the residential cycle is turning — home loan disbursements at ₹2,59,000 cr are holding up only because rates have fallen to 8.12%. Gold in INR at ₹13,518/gram (100th percentile) is the quiet hedge that institutional India is running alongside its equity exposure.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three risks, ranked by probability times impact. First: Brent at $97.21 — up from $88.82 six months ago — sustaining above $95 adds approximately ₹24,000 cr to India's monthly import bill, widens CAD by 40bps per $10, and forces the RBI to choose between defending INR and continuing its rate-cut cycle; fuel inflation at 27.41% (100th percentile) has not yet fed fully into core. Second: CD ratio at 83.04% with NBFC credit growth decelerating to 13% from 17% — if deposit growth stays at 10.8% while credit demand holds at 13.8%, the regulator's next move is macro-prudential tightening via risk weights, not rate policy. Third: BOJ at 1.0% with US 10Y sticky at 4.77% — yen carry unwind pressure on EM flows is not priced into India VIX at 11.16 (6th percentile). Watch Friday's US CPI print — at 3.30% headline with core PCE flat at 3.34%, any upside surprise resets the Fed pause narrative and the entire EM carry trade simultaneously.

"}
